chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Last appearances before retirement and the South Bay festival
summary: She stopped in 1957 but did the South Bay Jazz Festival in July 1958; Cliff encouraged her.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Okay, you did make that - you made actually two last appearances then. You say you stopped in '57, '58?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
But in July of '58 you did that South Bay Jazz Festival?

Oh yeah, oh yeah, but by that time I had - oh, I didn't tell you. When I was out in Honolulu I worked at a club there and on Sundays they had jam sessions. So there seemed to be quite a few American musicians who had made Honolulu their home. And there were quite a few female musicians out there. One gal, Ina Rae I didn't even know her name, had been with the Button's band. The all-girl band. So she showed up at the club one Sunday and she sang and after she sang a couple of numbers she picked up a trumpet and started playing the trumpet. I said to myself, you know that's a good idea, you know. Because as a singer you sing a couple of songs and then what do you do for encore? So I came back and I said to Cliff, you know I think I'll get a horn. I didn't know what I wanted to get. I didn't want to get a trumpet because I just figured that was going to be hard to play. And I didn't want a slide trombone because you know, that's like a circus. So it dawned on me that Billy Eckstine at one time played trombone. So I said

that's for me. So I said to Cliff, I said, if you're downtown because he was working at the time, I said, stop into Mannys and see if you can find me a trombone. So he did.
Pardon me. How long had you been married to Cliff?

Well, eight years, around seven or eight years, 1950 to 1957. So he stopped in at Mannys and said Maxine wants a valve Trombone. So Manny said a guy just walked in here yesterday with a valvetrombone and he said it's $65 so Cliff came back and told me. I told him to go and get it so he brought it home wrapped up in newspaper and we had a friend that lives up here in the Bronx, Herb Branch, a very good teacher, a very good trumpet player. He was retired. So he took me over there and I took lessons and Rex Stewart was promoting some of my jazz things out in Long Island somewhere and they had these tent jazz shows out there. And so I went out. I was invited to go out there and Rex came by and I sang a few things. the Willy/Lion, Cliff Jackson and a bunch of other people, and I said I'm going to take my valvetrombone. So I appeared and I don't even

know who the MC was, Leonard or what. But anyway he introduced me and I played "Do You Know What It Means For Miss New Orleans". And I think John Wilson said, she plays the valve trombone like she sings but I wish she would stick to singing. So that was that. That was the end of my valve trombone playing career. That didn't stop me though. I used to take it along with me hoping somebody would ask me to play. And even if they didn't, when the band would play "the Saints", you know, I would get my horn out anyway.
